text.p: Striker Florian Maurice, whose long-term injury has prevented World Cup hosts France from giving him a proper test in their problem position, has good news for coach Aime Jacquet.
Maurice, who ruptured his Achilles tendon playing in a league match at Nantes six months ago, is fit enough to have been included in Lyon's squad for a friendly with St Etienne on Friday.

Jacquet, looking for an attacking formula capable of helping France win the World Cup, is waiting patiently for Maurice's return to top flight action after giving him his first cap against Mexico three days before the devastating injury.

"I appreciated the telephone call Jacquet gave me after my operation (on September 5), as well as his recent words saying he was still counting on me. It's good for morale," the 23-year-old striker said.

Maurice's bad luck stands in stark contrast to the fortunes of Robert Pires, the Metz foward who also earned a first cap against Mexico after the pair's fine performances for the French under-21 and Olympic sides.
Pires, a substitute in the 2-1 home win over the Netherlands in midweek when he scored the equaliser, now has five caps and two goals as World Cup credentials.
He has played in all France's post-Euro 96 matches, as a substitute in four and in the starting line-up against Portugal last month.
Maurice's return to first division action is planned for Lyon's home match against Guingamp in two weeks time.

He hopes to be included in Jacquet's squad for the World Cup warm-up Tournoi de France in June. Jacquet could also select Maurice alongside Pires in the remaining friendly before the tournament at home to Sweden on April 2.
